claim:
The default source is `https://github.com/<repository>/releases/download/<tag>` from the manifest;
`--source URL|DIR` replaces that base. The asset name is appended to it. Redirects preserve Range.
Explicit `http://` sources are supported for local testing; use HTTPS for public mirrors. Each
logical read is split at asset boundaries and at `--range-bytes` (default 1 MiB, maximum 8 MiB). The
reader also fetches the header, footer, complete LDIR/PDIR, EXMT and RAYS. The decoder derives all
tower/action chunks and all chunks of each selected representative from that metadata. A coordinate
is not a same-index stored leaf: it needs its whole representative. Comma-separated coordinates and
inclusive ranges are accepted (for example `--coordinates 0,128` or `0-3,128`); duplicates are
removed and output order is increasing. Contiguous selections use their range filenames.
Noncontiguous selections write `cN.raw-selected.balls`, with their indices in
`decode.provenance.json`'s `coordinate_indices`. These are raw enclosures; normalization needs the
complete ray. `sic-container read-range` writes raw bytes to stdout and transfer statistics to
stderr; its arbitrary output range is a debugging facility, while opening the container still runs
the reader's metadata checks.

claim:
At most `--range-jobs` requests run concurrently (default 4, range 1..32). The default
range size is 1 MiB. Each range request
requires **206** and the exact `Content-Range: bytes FIRST-LAST/PART_SIZE`; a 200 response is aborted
at its headers. Wrong ranges, sizes, encodings and malformed redirects fail immediately. Connection
failures, timeouts and HTTP 408/429/5xx retry with exponential backoff (100 ms initially,
`--remote-retries 3` additional attempts, maximum 10). `--remote-timeout-ms` defaults to 30000 per
attempt; the connection timeout is 10000 ms, and stalled bodies also have a low-speed timeout.
Within a retry, a received prefix is retained and the next Range starts at the next byte. Across
process interruptions, complete atomic cache extents survive; at most the in-flight extents need
fetching again. The decoder reserves source staging and metadata headroom inside `--memory-mib`:
`2*jobs*(range_bytes+56) + 2*8 MiB + 512*cache_max_ranges + 8 MiB`, in addition to its measured
resident baseline and admitted numerical work. This is conservative (about 160 MiB at the defaults),
so tiny remote budgets require smaller range/job/metadata caps or are refused before decoding.
The resident set size remains subject to allocator and library overhead. `--check-budget` uses the operating
system's process high-water resident set size. For finalization it checks again after private validation
and whole-file SHA-256, before publishing, and reports the peak through publication.
This measure covers the process rather than filesystem cache or cgroup-wide memory.
Linux publication links the checked file descriptor without replacing an output.
Other platforms use the private pathname, with inode checks on either side of publication.
`--cache-max-ranges` bounds cache and read-plan metadata
(default 262144, maximum 1048576); exceeding it recommends a full download.

claim:
`--prefetch-mib` (default 8, 0 disables, maximum 256) controls physical-order lookahead to the disk
cache. One background scheduler shares demand's staging and request limits; it retains no decoded
chunks. It merges adjacent ranges and gaps up to `--coalesce-gap` bytes (default 4096, maximum 8 MiB),
never crossing a part boundary or the request-size cap. Gap bytes count toward the transfer plan.
The lookahead does not accumulate whole rays in RAM. Quiescing after decode makes the `REMOTE`
transfer/request/buffer statistics final; destruction cancels speculative HTTP and retries.

claim:
The default cache is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/sicx`, or `$HOME/.cache/sicx`; `--cache DIR` overrides it.
The sparse cache stores independent extents, not a partial SICX file:

`sic-construct 1 --out d2.sicx --radicals data/d2/d2.sicrad` reads this record (the default uses the
embedded pinned record). `sic-certify-stabilizer STABFILE --catalogue FILE --d2-exact data/d2/d2.sicrad` checks the
symmetries in dimension 2 exactly. The optional exact-JSON check with PARI/GP also exercises the
SICX file of dimension 2; its embedding limitations are stated in verification. The parsed
polynomial identities above are the mathematical basis of the radical proof, distinct from the
supplementary Arb residual.

CMake 3.20 or newer and a C++20 compiler are required. The default test-enabled build also requires
Node.js 20 or newer, Bash 4 or newer, and `nm` or `llvm-nm`. A build configured with
`-DSIC_BUILD_TESTS=OFF` needs only the build dependencies.

Set the consumer's `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` to the installation prefix and any separate dependency
prefixes. See the [library API](library.md) for components and ownership rules. Tests are enabled by
default. Test hooks require a separate build with `SIC_ENABLE_TEST_HOOKS=ON`; installation from that
build is refused. See [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for validation.

Build with C++20. `find_package(sic REQUIRED COMPONENTS core)` provides `sic::core` without FLINT.
The `support` and `search` components are also available without FLINT. A FLINT-enabled installation
additionally provides components and targets `sicx`, `decode`, `transport`, `access`, `bounds` and
`data`. The `data` component is also available without FLINT; exact decoding requires FLINT. These
resolve FLINT and optional HDF5 on the consumer host. HTTP access loads the libcurl ABI by its
loader name (`SIC_CURL_SONAME`, default `libcurl.so.4`); the host loader search path determines its
location. The core does not link curl or FLINT. Producer and decoder source identity definitions
are not exported to consumers.

`ResourceLimits` separates reader/writer resource policy from SICX 1.0 wire limits. Pass the same
policy to writer and reader when raising defaults. `ValuationPolicy` admits each dense table and
their total; verification uses the same estimator. `PrecisionPolicy` and decoder `maximum_precision`
are computational limits. BALL retains its normative maximum of 1024 limbs, independently of
informative working precision. A higher computational ceiling does not widen the wire format.
`InputLimits` configures core text input. HDF5 reads admit dimensions and vector bytes through the
default `InputLimits` before allocation. `RemoteOptions::limits` configures transport resource
bounds.
reason: Refers to library policies without stating their omitted numeric values.

claim:
`sic/support/parse_number.hpp` provides `sic::support::parse_number<T>(text, name,
kind, low, high, base)` for signed and unsigned integers and finite floating values.
Bounds are inclusive and default to the native type's limits. Conversion consumes
the entire string, is locale independent, and rejects overflow, whitespace and a
leading plus; signed values may have a leading minus. Integer bases are 2–36
(default 10), without prefixes; floating values use decimal general format.
Callers retain format tokenization and canonical spelling checks. Use
`ErrorKind::invalid_argument` for options and `invalid_format` for file or wire
records. Failures throw `sic::Error`. The installed `sic/support/cli.hpp`
`number<T>` facade retains its default lower bound of zero, `UsageError` subtype
and usage exit code 2.

in Release and RelWithDebInfo; disable it with `-DSIC_ENABLE_LTO=OFF`. Other configurations and sanitizer
builds do not enable LTO. Independent checker executables use LTO within each

claim:
`BallVerificationLimits` has defaults of 256 working bits, 64 absolute radius bits, maximum 4096
working bits, maximum dimension 2048, 64 Mi total input midpoint bits, 512 MiB admitted workspace
and a 10,000,000,000 work score. Callers may raise the dimension and precision limits up to
`LONG_MAX/2` and `sic::kNativeMaximumPrecision`, respectively, subject to work and workspace
admission. Dimension is at least 2. Working precision is at least 64 bits, with requested absolute
radius accuracy in 1..working_bits-32. Exceeding any limit throws.

This is engineering work admission, not a native-instruction bound or a
bit-complexity theorem for FLINT. The default score admits dimension 2048, including
its 4,194,303 nonidentity labels. Lower caller scores still refuse explicitly.

`components.hpp` separates generator selection, exact representation transformations, rescaling, and
the SICX writer. The native defaults are conjugate alignment, no representation transformations, the
shared greedy dyadic rule, and the shared SICX writer. `--generator-selector step-selection` selects
the step-selection presentation. Nonempty representation transformations and nondefault native
rescaling rules are explicitly refused until their required written-output checks are implemented.
`NoRescalingRule` exists as an internal interface/conformance control.
reason: Reviewed native component selection and representation behavior; source constructor and CLI selection are bound explicitly.

claim:
`sic-container reencode IN OUT [--threads N]` is the identity file route: `stored_element_source`
plus the inverse recorded dyadic shifts, recomputation of the shared default rescaling, and checked
serialization. It preserves all chunks, physical grouping and optional records byte for byte. Its
preflight includes both Reader caches, directory/metadata growth, codec windows, valuation tables
and inverse-tree scratch. Tests reject noncanonical C and insufficient budgets. This route preserves
the tower presentation and accepts no nonempty representation transformations or nondefault
rescaling rules.
reason: Representation identity contract, not a literal omitted-option value.

claim:
Default library producer threads use distinct physical cores in the process CPU
allowance, capped by cgroup CPU quotas/cpusets and SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK. The producer command-line tool
also applies its dimension-dependent work cap; the decoder command-line tool caps its default
at 32. Linux topology is cached once per CPU for the process lifetime. On macOS, logical
allowance uses hw.logicalcpu (hardware_concurrency() as fallback) and physical defaults
use hw.physicalcpu (or one). Other platforms without affinity use hardware_concurrency()
for logical allowance and one physical core for defaults. Unknown Linux cgroup-v2
ancestry limits defaults to one worker only. Memory discovery still fails closed.
Malformed readable quotas are errors.

Explicit SIC_THREADS in the library and --threads in the producer command-line tool take precedence
over the default and are never clamped to the CPU allowance; invalid counts are refused.
Decoder teams retain the requested count, subject to `maximum_threads` and memory
admission. Physical compute dispatch uses a subset on distinct placement cores when
placement CPUs are known; otherwise it uses the full team. There is no process-allowance
cap on explicit counts. Internal producer fan-out uses its caller's worker budget,
bounded by available work and memory.
Snapshot::cpus retains logical allowance and SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU accounting. The production command-line tool
captures its options, validates documented inherited producer settings, and clears inherited
SIC_* settings before running the producer. Invalid unused settings are refused before output
probes or construction work.
Complete syntax and option defaults are generated in [Command-line tools](tools.md).
reason: Links the generated help reference; no additional default value is stated.

claim:
The default worker ceiling follows the analytic grid size (1 worker through d4, then d/4 through
d128, 32 at d256, and at most 64 thereafter), bounded by the process CPU allowance. An explicit
`--threads` uses the requested limit, subject to memory admission. Class concurrency adapts to
remaining classes, free worker shares and fully charged owner forecasts; each completed owner
releases its admission before queued work can reuse it.

The selector’s complete incremental budget defaults to 16384 MiB; optional
cache ceilings, batch and worker budgets constrain it further. Cache mode is
used only when both the complete incremental and global live sets fit;
`--alignment-cache-mib 0` forces deterministic replay. Search parameters,
base candidates and exact conjugates enter PROV and authenticated resume
journals; changing the semantic plan refuses resume. Resource-only retention
choices do not enter that semantic plan. `--log-admissions` records decisions.
Do not interpret an admission refusal as a mathematical disproof.

For any supported exponent S ≥ 2, run `sic-construct S --orders` to get the
construction orders and their conductors, sorted by increasing conductor.
The standard order has discriminant (d+1)(d−3). The maximal order removes
its square factor. When the discriminant is squarefree the two coincide,
and the command lists a single standard-order row. Give each distinct order
to `sic-construct S --order ORDER`. The default order is standard in every dimension.
Number the rows m1, m2, and so on. The order, dimension and resource flags are
all the producer needs to construct the exact part.

The default S=1 source is the embedded pinned radical record. To use the
explicit identical input, add `--radicals data/d2/d2.sicrad`.
Its parsed coefficients must satisfy positivity, A+2B=1, 4AB=1/3 and
(A−2B)^2=1/3; these are exact identities in Q(√3), not residual tests.
An independent exact stabilizer check reads the radical input directly:

Implementation resource limits MUST be checked before allocation or expansion.
The reference defaults are: integer magnitude at most `2^20` bytes; any JSON
chunk at most 64 MiB; decoded logical leaf and decoded physical chunk at most
256 MiB; at most `2^24` entries in each directory; JSON nesting at most 32;
integer strings at most 18 digits except `scale`; no unbounded recursion
from input. These are resource refusals and may be raised explicitly, not
silently bypassed. Declared lengths MUST NOT force whole-file allocation.
A partial reader can defer payload-wide checks, but never a failed check on
bytes it actually uses. Precision/resource refusal MUST be distinguishable
from successful verification and from proved algebraic inconsistency.

claim:
Build with `cmake -S cpp -B cpp/build -DSIC_ENABLE_FLINT=ON`, then `cmake --build cpp/build --target
sic-certify-norm`; the binary is `cpp/build/sic-certify-norm`. Use
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=FLINT_INSTALL` if FLINT is installed outside the system search path.
See the complete [norm checker options](tools.md#sic-certify-norm) for syntax and defaults.
`--estimate` performs exact preprocessing and a precision estimate without a SIC-POVM verdict;
`--leaf-estimate` gives a heuristic feasibility estimate without exact preprocessing or a SIC-POVM
verdict. Exit codes are 0 for all selected rays certified (or a completed estimate), 1 for an
inconclusive certificate or BALL mismatch, 2 for usage errors, and 3 for a refused input or
computation. Numeric command-line values must be full-string unsigned decimals with checked overflow;
malformed values, missing values and out-of-range options exit 2 before certification. `--max-bits`
accepts
1..9223372036854775807, `--ray` accepts a zero-based index, and `--threads` must be positive.
Input-only limits include 64 MiB per directory/JSON payload and 256 MiB per physical/logical
payload; see the checker input/admission contract below for the other limits. Mathematical
certification requires `d, [L:K] ≤ 4096`; these are resource limits, not feasibility guarantees.
Exact certification supports real quadratic base fields and quadratic tower levels at the final
high-precision stage. Odd levels can be used for estimates, but final certification refuses them.
Exact-only files can be read for estimates; certification requires finalized rays and balls.
reason: The complete generated norm-checker help owns option defaults; this paragraph links to it and describes estimate/exit scope. Semantic default comparisons use that generated help, and compiled omitted-option controls remain enrolled.

claim:
`ctest -L crt` exercises eleven input groups (valid, rejection mutations, boundaries/regrouping,
partial trust/scope, amendments, primitive guards, mixed odd/quadratic branches, targeted guards,
general dimensions, deterministic fuzz mutations, and public command-line interface), five fixture CRT proofs,
bound-only diagnostics, strict command-line option and error cases, help/parser defaults, help, source
independence, a shift retry, and three deliberate mathematical negative controls. The independent
executables are enrolled in the repository’s independence audit. Rehashed negative fixtures pin
rejection categories so a different later failure cannot silently substitute for the intended check.
Five additional `sic-test-crt-faults` cases interpose OS/FLINT failures to test otherwise rare
fail-closed paths; interposition is test-only.
reason: Lists default-check test coverage; no numeric default is stated.

claim:
Default input limits are `d <= 4096`, `D <= 65536`, 4,194,304 total dense
coordinates, 64 MiB per directory/JSON payload, 256 MiB per physical/logical
payload, one MiB per integer, JSON depth 32 and 1,048,576 JSON nodes. Branch
precision, branch mantissa bits and branch exponent magnitude are limited to
`2^20`; exact algebraic operations use degree 256 and height `2^20`.
`ReadOptions::algebraic_limits` can lower those two budgets. Component extraction,
trace contraction, trace-dual construction, integer/dyadic scaling and polynomial
root isolation have conservative pre-expansion degree/height bounds and result
checks. Admission may refuse a calculation whose eventual minimal polynomial
would fit; the reader never expands first and relies only on a later size check.
The two dimension
limits can be raised with `--max-dimension` and `--max-field-dimension`, and
allocation limits are explicit in `ReadOptions`. The mathematical certificate
requires `d,D <= 4096` and real-base-field restrictions; input-only
verification accepts `d=2`. No mathematical algorithm or precision policy is
changed by raising an input limit.

The default algebraic-fallback resource limit is tower degree 256; the certified interval path does
not require a full compositum. The limit can be raised explicitly with `--branch-degree-limit`
(maximum 2^20). Further reader resource limits are: branch precision and absolute exponents 2^20;
branch strings 1 MiB; exact coefficient support 2^18 and bit height 16,384; conservative retained
BALL admission 1 GiB, including declared midpoint width and allocation headroom; rescaling weight
keys 2^24; text lines 256 MiB. The spec's 64 MiB JSON, 256 MiB physical payload, 2^24 directory
entries, 2^20-byte integer magnitudes and nesting 32 limits also apply. Files beyond a resource
limit return refusal, never PASS. Large actual presentations can therefore require a higher limit or
be refused.

6. **Resources come from the process allowance.** Derive default threads and
   memory budgets from process affinity and cgroup/job limits, never host totals.
   Explicit settings take precedence; memory admission fails closed. Platforms
   without an affinity API use OS logical/physical CPU counts (on macOS,
   `hw.logicalcpu`/`hw.physicalcpu`). The logical count falls back to
   `hardware_concurrency()` and the physical count to 1.
   One function owns CPU allowance; cache topology once per process.
   `sic_test_policy_newton_workers` checks that the Newton table takes class
   workers from their owner; review checks the allowance, topology and admission rules.

claim:
Ordinary tests, including policy tests and default heavy controls, have a
positive timeout of at most 120 seconds. The sole long-test exemption is
`sic_test_sicx_exact_gp_d16`: explicitly opt in with `SIC_SICX_GP_D16=ON`;
it is heavy and retains a 3600-second timeout (one PARI/GP shift takes several
minutes empirically). Its registration is checked without requiring the long
computation. Use `ctest -L independence` for checker boundaries, or
`ctest -LE heavy` for the ordinary suite. The publication manifest pins the
copied test inputs.
reason: Timeout and optional heavy membership are checked by the registry.

claim:
`SIC_TEST_WORKERS` is an optional positive CMake cache integer. When unset or
empty, the parallel-product test discovers its process CPU allowance at run time
and uses `max(3, allowance)` native FLINT workers. The hooks install-refusal test
uses the same runtime default for nested build jobs. An explicit value (for
example `-DSIC_TEST_WORKERS=8`) is honoured unchanged and never capped. The
parallel-product coverage guard fails loudly below three workers; even a
one-CPU test process exercises helper leases. Tile requests `{1,2,8,16,32}` and
explicit worker lists in other controls retain their values. Run oversubscribed
controls with `ctest -j1`. Use atomic `mkdtemp` directories for scratch paths
shared across process namespaces, or paths scoped to the configured CTest build
directory.
Tests requiring an optional external program must report SKIPPED with a clear
reason when it is unavailable, and use its configured executable path when available.
reason: Runtime worker discovery and explicit override are checked by the registry.

claim:
On glibc, `sic-construct` sets the process heap trim threshold to 16 MiB and the
mmap threshold to 32 MiB before starting construction threads. Ordinary frees
can then release free top chunks in worker arenas while medium-sized temporaries
remain on the heap. If mmap threshold setup is refused, the command-line tool skips trim setup
and continues with allocator defaults. If trim setup is refused, it continues
with the mmap setting. Any environment
variable whose name starts with `MALLOC_`, or any colon-separated entry starting
with `glibc.malloc.` in `GLIBC_TUNABLES`, disables the entire command-line default, including
when its value is empty. This includes unrelated allocator settings such as
`MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` and `glibc.malloc.tcache_count`.
